page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics consistently fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, reaching 514.76 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 45.33 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% at 27.85 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations are accelerated by hardware flags including AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and AVX.

This instance offers balanced resource density, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require steady, dedicated CPU performance without the premium of specialized memory or compute-heavy hardware. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, Redis database operations, and light software compilation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU performance alongside average multi-core and memory bandwidth results, though multi-threaded decompression represents a minor performance tradeoff. Supported by hardware-accelerated cryptography and vector extensions, this instance is a cost-effective, balanced choice for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, Redis deployments, and moderate software compilation.
